blogs.title: More Than Just B12: When Nutritional Deficiency Masks a Genetic Disaster
blogs.description: A deep dive into the diagnostic trap of 'satisficing.' This post discusses how severe vitamin B12 deficiency can provide a convenient explanation for pancytopenia and neuropathy, potentially leading clinicians to overlook a deeper, multisystem genetic pathology like Telomere Biology Disorders (TBDs) when the clinical picture remains disproportionately severe after supplementation.

blogs.title: Beyond the Triad: Rethinking the Presentation of Dyskeratosis Congenita
blogs.description: Traditional teaching emphasizes the mucocutaneous triad (leukoplakia, nail dystrophy, and skin pigmentation) for diagnosing Dyskeratosis Congenita. This post explores the 'incomplete' phenotypes of TBDs, highlighting how these disorders can manifest in adulthood as isolated pulmonary fibrosis, liver cirrhosis, or bone marrow failure without any of the classic skin or nail findings.

blogs.title: The Cost of Division: Why Telomere Disorders Hit the Lungs, Liver, and Marrow
blogs.description: An exploration of the pathophysiology of TBDs. This post explains the concept of 'replicative stress' and why high-turnover tissues—specifically hematopoietic stem cells, alveolar epithelium, and hepatocytes—are the primary targets of telomere attrition, leading to the unique constellation of organ fibrosis and cytopenias.

blogs.title: VUS or Verdict? Navigating Genetic Uncertainty in Rare Disease
blogs.description: Clinical exome sequencing often returns a 'Variant of Uncertain Significance' (VUS). This post discusses the clinical tension of integrating a VUS into a diagnosis, arguing for a 'clinical-first' approach where the phenotype (premature aging, multi-organ fibrosis) can help upgrade the significance of a genetic variant in the context of rare diseases like PARN mutations.

blogs.title: The Young Adult with an Old Body: A Framework for Premature Aging Syndromes
blogs.description: How do you approach a 20-something presenting with osteoporosis, grey hair, and organ fibrosis? This post provides a differential diagnosis framework for clinicians encountering 'accelerated aging' in young adults, contrasting TBDs with other progeroid syndromes and autoimmune mimics.
